about: workflow:read-my-device-notices: reads the notices queued or positively delivered to one registered device (a browser, a phone, the Mac app or a watch), oldest first after its cursor, read straight from the person's own store (rule a-tool-is-only-what-the-store-cannot-do). It replaces tool:my-device-notices in tools/tell-the-person, which read the device registration and the told-the-person records through the retired records door. Nothing here writes: the cursor is answered, and the device that reads keeps it.

payload.label: Read the notices ready for one of my devices
payload.job: Read the notices ready for one registered device of the person (its route: live, web-push or apns), only those queued or positively delivered to that device, oldest first after its cursor, with the cursor the device should keep next.
payload.produces: The next notices for one registered device, oldest first, and the cursor to keep, read from the person's own store and answered as it was kept.

source.from: tools/tell-the-person read-data/told.mjs (myDeviceNotices, keptNotices, resultFor, channelRoute) and tool:my-device-notices, read on trillion-workshop origin/main 75fa3807fc
source.note: The device registration is kept where the store keeps notification devices; the device's own registration writes it, and this recipe only reads it. The cursor rule (stop before a notice whose delivery to this route is still being attempted) and the device scoping (exact device_ids receipts, or the live fallback for a legacy channel-wide queue) are written out in the answer step.

where.description: Where the person keeps these things: the store's own address

language.description: How that store is spoken to, in its own terms

credential_name.description: The vault name of the login the run uses, when it needs one

channel.description: The channel to read for: device-pull, mac-app, mac-voice, web-push or apns (default: device-pull for a live device, else the device's route)

after.description: The cursor the device kept: only notices with a seq above it (default 0)

steps.title: Read what the store already keeps
steps.do: Speak to the store in its own language, with the login under its credential_name, and read its own description of what it holds. Submit where the told notices are kept (told_kept_in, or null), where the notification device registrations are kept (device_kept_in, or null), and the names of the objects that keep them.

steps.title: Prove the device reading on the example notices
steps.do: In a throwaway place in the same store, with the same objects, keep these example registrations and notices. Registrations: device-a {device_id: "device-a", route: "live"}; browser-a {device_id: "browser-a", route: "web-push"}; phone-a {device_id: "phone-a", route: "apns"}; late-device {device_id: "late-device", route: "live", added_at: "2026-02-01T00:00:00Z"}. Notices, one per seq, each at "2026-01-01T00:0<seq>:00Z", kind "report", title "Notice <seq>", with these results: seq 1 {device-pull: {sent: true, stage: "queued"}}; seq 2 {web-push: {sent: true, device_ids: ["browser-a"]}}; seq 3 {apns: {sent: true, device_ids: ["phone-a"]}}; seq 4 {web-push: {sent: true, device_ids: ["browser-b"]}}; seq 5 {device-pull: {sent: false, stage: "unavailable"}}; seq 6 {web-push: {sent: false, stage: "attempting"}}. Then answer these reads from those only. (1) device-a, channel mac-app, after 0: the notice told:1 only, cursor 6, said "1 notice is ready for this device, oldest first.". (2) device_id nobody: refused with "This device is not registered to read notices.". (3) browser-a, no channel, after 0: the notice told:2 only, cursor 5 (it stops before told:6, still attempting), said "1 notice is ready for this device, oldest first.". (4) phone-a, no channel, after 0: told:3 only, cursor 6, said "1 notice is ready for this device, oldest first.". (5) browser-a with channel apns: refused with "channel apns does not match this registered device route.". (6) late-device, channel device-pull, after 0: no notices, cursor 6, said "0 notices are ready for this device, oldest first." (the registration was added after every notice it could have had). Then remove the throwaway place. Submit answers: one per read, in order, as above.

steps.title: Answer the notices ready for this device
steps.do: Read the device registration of input.device_id from where the store keeps notification devices. Trim input.device_id. When there is no registration, or its route is not live, web-push or apns, refuse: "This device is not registered to read notices.". Work out the channel: input.channel trimmed when given, else device-pull when the route is live, else the route. The channel's route is live for device-pull, mac-app and mac-voice, web-push for web-push, and apns for apns; when the channel's route is not the device's route, refuse: "channel <channel> does not match this registered device route.". The cursor input.after is a whole number from 0 (default 0). The limit is input.limit (default 20, at most 100). Read the told_the_person objects (when there are any; else none) in seq order. A notice counts when its seq is above the cursor and it has a result for this channel: that result is results[channel], or, for mac-app only, results["device-pull"]. A notice with a result whose device_ids list is present counts when that list includes this device_id. Otherwise it counts when the channel is live and the result has sent true or stage "queued", and the device was not added after the notice (added_at is later than the notice's at). Take the first limit counted notices, oldest first. Each one is answered as {id: "told:<seq>", seq, kind, title (or ""), body (or ""), open (or null), at (or null), read (true only when read is true), actions (the item's actions when a list, else []), level (the item's level, else "active"), group (only when it has one), read_on (only when it has one)}. The cursor starts at the input's after. Walk every notice above after in seq order: stop at the first whose result for this channel has stage "checking" or "attempting"; otherwise the cursor becomes that notice's seq when it is higher. When the shown notices reach the limit, the cursor becomes the smaller of itself and the last shown notice's seq. Answer {device_id, channel, cursor, notices, said} where said is "<n> notice is ready for this device, oldest first." when n is 1, and "<n> notices are ready for this device, oldest first." otherwise. Nothing is written.
